subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicit keys from `skills.entries.<skill>.env` be allowed to bypass the sensitive-name block for host exec inheritance, while still blocking dangerous host-runtime variables and sandbox propagation?
rationale: This is not just a mechanical bug fix: it changes which credential-shaped config values an allowed exec command can receive, so the permanent security boundary needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Allow explicit host-only skill env
options.body: Treat user-configured per-skill env keys as an explicit host-run allowlist, retain dangerous variable blocks, and require regression tests for host exec plus sandbox isolation.

options.title: Keep metadata-only sensitive env
options.body: Preserve the current sensitive-key block unless the skill metadata declares the key, and update docs or the gog skill metadata to make the supported path clear.

options.title: Adopt the linked candidate after repair
options.body: Have a maintainer repair or replace the conflicting linked fix branch, then review it against the security-boundary tests before merge.

recommendation.title: Allow explicit host-only skill env
recommendation.body: Treat user-configured per-skill env keys as an explicit host-run allowlist, retain dangerous variable blocks, and require regression tests for host exec plus sandbox isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest history signal is recent merged work on skill env isolation and credential handling around child process boundaries.
